facts.statement: The dinosaur was named and described in 2014 as Datanglong guangxiensis by Mo Jinyou, Zhou Fusheng, Li Guangning, Hunag Zhen, and Cao Chenyun.
facts.quote: The dinosaur was named and described in 2014 as Datanglong guangxiensis, by Mo Jinyou, Zhou Fusheng, Li Guangning, Hunag Zhen and Cao Chenyun.

facts.statement: The species is known from a single holotype specimen, GMG 00001, consisting of vertebrae and hip bones.
facts.quote: Datanglong guangxiensis is known from one specimen, holotype GMG 00001, which encompasses vertebrae and hip bones.

facts.statement: Datanglong was a large predatory theropod reaching a length of roughly 8 to 9 meters.
facts.quote: Datanglong is a large predatory theropod with a length of roughly 8 to 9 m.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the holotype specimen is about 0.7 meters.
facts.quote: The specimen has a preserved length of about 0.7 m.

facts.statement: The last dorsal vertebra features a pleurocoel, or pneumatic cavity, bounded by enlarged posterior ridges and the vertebral body.
facts.quote: The last dorsal vertebra has a pleurocoel, or pneumatic cavity, that is bounded by an enlarged posterior ridge between the diapophysis and the vertebral body, by the posterior ridge between the parapophysis and the vertebral body; and by the vertebral body itself.

facts.statement: The groove on the underside of the rear ilium blade, which attaches the musculus caudofemoralis brevis, is shallow with a short, ridge-shaped inner surface.
facts.quote: The groove in the underside of the rear blade of the ilium, serving as an attachment to the musculus caudofemoralis brevis, is shallow and the "brevis shelf", the inner surface of the medial blade wall uncovered by it, is short and shaped like a ridge.

facts.statement: The last dorsal vertebra resembles Ceratosauria because its parapophysis extends beyond the diapophysis.
facts.quote: The last dorsal vertebra resembles those of the Ceratosauria in that the parapophysis, the lower rib joint process, extends beyond the diapophysis, the upper rib joint process.

facts.statement: Datanglong lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Albian) in the Xinlong Formation of what is now Guangxi, China.
facts.quote: It existed during Xinlong Formation, Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Albian), in what is now Guangxi China.

facts.statement: Datanglong is classified as an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod with uncertain taxonomic placement.
facts.quote: Datanglong is an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod of uncertain taxonomic placement.

facts.statement: Datanglong is classified within the unranked family Carcharodontosauria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Carcharodontosauria

facts.statement: Datanglong belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Andrea Cau suggested that the initial analysis focusing on basal Tetanurae might have misplaced basal coelurosaurians.
facts.quote: Soon after the publication, the Italian paleontologist Andrea Cau pointed out that this analysis had been strongly focused on the basal Tetanurae and therefore contained few traits of the Coelurosauria. That carried the danger that basal coelurosaurians were misplaced.

facts.statement: In 2017, Samathi and Chanthasit reported finding Datanglong nested within Megaraptora, sharing ilium pneumaticity with other megaraptorans.
facts.quote: In 2017, Adun Samathi and Phorphen Chanthasit reported in an SVP abstract that they found Datanglong to nest in Megaraptora, "sharing the pneumaticity of the ilium with other megaraptorans."

facts.statement: In 2024, Samathi and colleagues recovered Datanglong within Coelurosauria and Megaraptora based on nine supporting characters.
facts.quote: In 2024, Samathi and colleagues recovered Datanglong in this position once again, identifying nine characters to support its placement within Coelurosauria and also Megaraptora.

facts.statement: In 2011, a team from the Geological Research Service Institute discovered the remains of an unknown large theropod near the village of Nazao, twenty kilometers southwest of Datang city in Guangxi, China.
facts.quote: En 2011, un equipo del Instituto del Servicio de Investigación Geológica encontró cerca del pueblo de Nazao, veinte kilómetros al suroeste de la ciudad de Datang, cerca de Nanning en Guangxi en China, los restos de un gran terópodo desconocido para la ciencia.

facts.statement: In 2014, the remains were described and named the type species Datanglong guangxiensis by Mo Jinyou, Zhou Fusheng, Li Guang Ning, and Cao Zhen Hunag Chenyun.
facts.quote: En 2014, estos restos fueron descritos y nombrados como la especie tipo Datanglong guangxiensis por Mo Jinyou, Zhou Fusheng, Li Guang Ning y Cao Zhen Hunag Chenyun.

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to the Datang basin with the Mandarin term long, meaning "dragon".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina una referencia a la cuenca de Datang con el término mandarín long, "dragón".

facts.statement: The species name refers to the Guangxi province.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a la provincia de Guangxi.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil, GMG 00001, was found in a layer of the Xinlong Formation, which dates to the Early Cretaceous, though its precise age is uncertain.
facts.quote: El fósil holotipo, GMG 00001, fue encontrado en una capa de la Formación Xinlong cuya edad precisa es incierta, pero data del Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a series of vertebrae starting with the fourteenth dorsal vertebra, extending through the five sacral vertebrae and ending with the second caudal vertebra, connected to the left ilion and upper parts of the left ischium and pubis, plus a piece of the right ilion.
facts.quote: Consiste de una serie de vértebras que inicia con la decimocuarta vértebra dorsal de la columna vertebral, de acuerdo con los descriptores, se extiende con las cinco vértebras del sacro y finaliza con la segunda vértebra caudal, conectándose con el ilion izquierdo y las partes superiores del isquion y el pubis izquierdos, y a una pieza del ilion derecho.

facts.statement: The authors of the description placed Datanglong within Carcharodontosauria in a basal position, using a previous cladistic analysis by Matthew Carrano.
facts.quote: Los autores de la descripción situaron a Datanglong dentro de Carcharodontosauria, en una posición basal, haciendo uso de un análisis cladístico anterior realizado por Matthew Carrano.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Andrea Cau argued that the previous analysis was too focused on basal Tetanurae and incorporated few traits of Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo italiano Andrea Cau señaló por su parte que este análisis estaba demasiado enfocado en los Tetanurae basales y por lo tanto incorporaba pocos rasgos de los Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: Cau included Datanglong characteristics in his own much more extensive analysis, which revealed that Datanglong would be a basal coelurosaurian.
facts.quote: Cau incorporó las características de Datanglong en su propio y mcuho más extenso análisis el cual reveló que Datanglong sería un celurosaurio basal.

facts.statement: If correct, it could be the first large-sized basal coelurosaurian.
facts.quote: De ser correcto, podría ser el primer celurosaurio basal de un tamaño realmente grande.

facts.statement: Cau noted that all synapomorphies Datanglong shares with Carcharodontosauria, such as pneumatic cavities in the ilion and the thin articulation between the ilion and ischium, are also shared with the Megaraptora group.
facts.quote: Él también llamó la atención sobre el hecho de que todas las sinapomorfias que comparte Datanglong con Carcharodontosauria como las cavidades neumáticas en el ilion y la delgada articulación entre el ilion y el isquion, también las comparte con el grupo Megaraptora.

facts.statement: The parent group of Datanglong is Carcharodontosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Carcharodontosauria

facts.statement: Datanglong is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The time range for Datanglong is from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago, during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
